findings.passage: “I am proud of what we were able to accomplish this session. We reduced the tax burden on Texas’ families and businesses, protected Voter ID and the integrity of our elections, slowed the growth of government, enacted public education reform, and passed pro-life, pro-family legislation for Texas.”
findings.note: Reelection announcement (2015) quoting Schofield; he lists protecting Voter ID among the session's achievements. Page is a PAC repost of his campaign release.

findings.passage: He passed legislation (along with Senator Paul Bettencourt) to make a birth certificate available at no charge to anyone who only needs it to get their voter ID card. This removes one of the phony arguments often made that Voter ID imposes additional costs on people attempting to vote.
findings.note: Text of his campaign release (issued in his name, reposted by a PAC) describing a law giving a free birth certificate to people who need it only to get a voter ID card.

findings.passage: “My view is, if you swore to us you’re not a citizen, off you go,” Schofield said. “We’ll take your word for it.”
findings.note: Quoted by Community Impact at a town hall; he describes his bill to remove from the voter rolls anyone who swears in a jury-duty affidavit that they are not a U.S. citizen.

findings.passage: I have asked to remain on the Elections and Judiciary & Civil Jurisprudence committees, so I can protect the fairness of our elections (including our Voter ID law) and defend the tort reform that has enabled our state’s economy to keep growing when other states have stagnated.
findings.note: Written answer in a Community Impact Q&A; he says he wants to stay on the Elections committee to protect the state's Voter ID law.

findings.motion: HB 1263, verification of citizenship of an applicant for voter registration
findings.note: Bill filed by Schofield. The secretary of state would check an applicant's citizenship with the Department of Public Safety. An applicant the department cannot confirm would have 60 days to give proof (passport, birth certificate with photo ID, or citizenship papers with photo ID). Referred to the Elections committee 2025-03-10; no later action shown.
subjects: documents accepted as proof of citizenship

findings.motion: HB 4507, federal election practices and procedures
findings.note: Bill filed by Schofield. It would let the secretary of state keep a separate federal-elections-only voter registration system if federal law changes registration rules, with certificates marked as valid for federal elections only. Reported out of the State Affairs committee 7 to 4 and placed on the General State Calendar 2021-05-12.
subjects: voter registration rules, federal versus state

findings.motion: HB 209, separation of federal elections from state and local elections
findings.note: Bill filed by Schofield on separating federal elections from state and local elections and related practices and procedures. Referred to State Affairs 2025-02-27; no later action shown.
